Fed's Barr: Central Bank Should Act Decisively to Raise Rates if Inflation Doesn't Appear to Be Moderating Sufficiently
Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said the central bank should act decisively to raise interest rates if inflation appears not to be moderating sufficiently.
Speaking at an event in Washington, D.C., Barr said there is a risk of broader price pressures taking hold as inflation has been above the Fed's preferred target range.

With the Fed's September interest rate meeting underway, Barr said if data trends give him confidence that inflation is moderating on a path to 2%, the Fed could take a 'bit more time' to assess their policy stance.
"However, if inflation appears not to be moderating sufficiently, then I think we should act decisively to raise rates," a published text of his remarks said.

Barr said a series of supply shocks, such as tariffs, the conflict in the Middle East and rapid AI buildout has pushed the Fed off course. In addition, Barr said core non-housing services inflation remains elevated.
